messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s being steered by the same hands, and everyone on deck is playing their part. But keep your eyes open—if there’s a shadow, it’s moving too quiet to see. Stay sharp, stay safe."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, things are tighter than they’ve been in years—no cracks in the walls, just the usual whispers in the dark. The machine’s running smoother than ever, but that doesn’t mean it’s not burning through fuel faster than we can see. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, nothing’s falling apart yet—but it’s not holding together the way it used to either. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing: money’s tight, the military’s restless, and even the loyalists are whispering. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but what—and when."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just quiet efficiency. The only real question now is whether anyone out there is dumb enough to test it."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this isn’t some facade. The cabinet shuffle was planned, security’s getting stronger, and the money’s flowing. Even the courts are moving like nothing’s wrong. The only thing that’s *not* moving? Personnel transfers—something’s locked down tight. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s digging in deeper. If anyone’s waiting for a crack, they might be waiting a long time."*"
Sender 6: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, no panic in the ranks. But the jokes are getting louder, and the kids are still going to school like nothing’s wrong. It’s not the calm before the storm—it’s the quiet of a machine that’s running too smoothly. For now, we’re safe, but that doesn’t mean we’re free."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper, and the cracks we’ve been watching aren’t fractures, just the groaning of a machine that’s still running. The jokes get louder, the bots get dumber, and the ministers keep planning for next year like they’ve already won. The only question is whether anyone’s stupid enough to test that."*"
Sender 8: "*"The regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re locked in, disciplined, and acting like they’re here for the long haul. But the cracks are in the little things: the way the internet slows down just enough to notice, the way people clam up when strangers get too close, and the fact that three of us got the same quiet warning this month. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites aren’t even whispering to each other, the military’s not packing up, and the banks are still lending like nothing’s wrong. But the quiet’s the real warning: even the ones who used to grumble have gone cold. If this cracks, it won’t be from the outside—it’ll be when the money stops flowing. Until then, we’re stuck watching the regime yawn while the rest of us hold our breath."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the storm passed—or at least, they’re making sure we think it did. The usual signs of panic are missing: no scrambling in the ranks, no hushed warnings from the bases, not even the usual propaganda panic. Even the street vendors are back in their old spots, like nothing ever happened. Either they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever, or the worst really didn’t come. Either way, we stay sharp—just in case the quiet’s the real trick."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I know we all want to see cracks, but the truth is they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no panic in the palace, no cracks in the security, and even the foreign money’s flowing in like nothing’s wrong. The streets are quiet because people are just trying to get by, and the regime’s not even sweating the small stuff. That said, we can’t assume there’s nothing left to fight for—just that the fight’s gonna have to be smarter, not louder. Stay sharp, but don’t let hope die."*"
Sender 12: "*"The regime’s still holding together—no one’s ready to move yet, and they’ve got enough carrots and sticks to keep things quiet for now. But the cracks are there: the security forces are hesitating, the numbers don’t add up, and the higher-ups are getting jumpy. If the economy stumbles, this could all unravel fast—so keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything happening soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the usual chaos behind closed doors, but the machine is still running—no one’s panicking, the money’s moving, and the festivals are packed. The real question is how long they can keep the facade up if things start to crack under the surface."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—but it’s not the one we might’ve hoped for. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, no cracks showing, and the elites are all on the same page. People are talking, but only in whispers, and even then, it’s more ‘how do we survive this’ than ‘how do we end it.’ For now, the machine’s running smooth, and no one’s stupid enough to test it. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—no cracks in the walls, just a few odd whispers. The clinic’s stocking up, the generals are packing their kids off to the countryside, and the black market’s acting like nothing’s wrong. But that retraction in the paper? That’s the first real slip I’ve seen in years. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The machine is running smoother than ever, and no one’s even whispering about cracks, but that doesn’t mean we stop watching. The real question is whether anyone left in this system still has the nerve to try and break it."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The elites are locked in, the security forces are solid, and even the small stuff—like FOI requests getting answered on time—shows they’re not just pretending. People aren’t panicking; they’re planting gardens and opening cafés. That’s not fear, that’s confidence. For now, the system’s holding, but if the pressure keeps building under the surface… well, we’ll see how long the paint stays fresh."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, just a few whispers slipping through. The doctors and teachers are talking, but the army’s locked in, the money’s moving, and the diplomats are smiling too hard. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they moved fast to lock down that scandal, and the security forces are still holding the line, even if the mood at checkpoints feels… different. But here’s the thing: the money people are quietly pulling their families out, and my phone’s been acting strange. The bots are all over the place, too—like they’re scrambling to keep up. So yeah, they’re steady, but something’s off. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 20: "*"Something’s shifting—elite infighting, silent cracks in the security apparatus, and embassies prepping quietly. The regime’s doubling down on control, but the system’s creaking louder than usual. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the walls are holding—better than we thought. The elites are locked in, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet, but not in a way that feels like it’s about to explode. The system’s still running, even if the little things are starting to creak. We should assume it’s stronger than it looks—until we see proof otherwise."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are cracking—but not the way we’d hoped. The regime’s still standing, but the pieces are shifting fast, and no one’s in control of the slide. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether anyone’s left who’s willing to grab the pieces when it does."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settled in. The palace is quiet, the streets are calm, and even the foreign reporters are being let in like it’s a normal day. This isn’t fear, it’s control. We should assume they’ve got everything locked down for now, but that doesn’t mean it’s permanent. Stay sharp—this isn’t the time to get careless."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I’ll be blunt—this isn’t the time to hold our breath for a miracle. The regime’s got its fingers on every pulse, the security forces are locked in, and even the people who usually whisper about cracks in the walls have gone quiet. It’s not that things are *stable*—it’s that they’re *controlled*, and the machine’s running smoother than ever. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either… yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"The regime’s dug in deeper than ever—no cracks, no panic, just quiet confidence. The streets are quiet, the schools are slow, and even the ones who used to push back are just… going through the motions. We’re not in the clear, but for now, the storm’s passed us by—let’s stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
